persona.bio: Owns a small women's clothing boutique, just her and two part timers. Working the floor, buying at markets twice a year, posting new arrivals on Instagram, steaming and tagging stock, window displays every month, payroll and paying vendors, answering DMs about sizes and holds. She does most of it on her iPhone between customers. Instagram and the DMs take the most time, then tagging stock. She uses ChatGPT some weeks for captions and Canva's AI for posts.

path.role: You run a small women’s clothing boutique with two part time helpers, handling customer messages, stock, and social posts yourself.

steps.note: I own a small women’s clothing boutique with two part time helpers, and I handle customer messages, new stock and social posts myself. I write to shoppers who message me about sizes, colors and holds, and I write Instagram captions for new pieces. My tone is warm, short and friendly, like a shop owner chatting with a regular. I like replies of one to three sentences and captions that sound like me. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, sizes, colors, fabrics or store hours. If something is missing, put it in square brackets and ask me. Never invent a policy. Always give me a draft I can read and change before it goes out.

steps.title: Your customer message replies, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each one a few letters away. You already answer the same questions about sizes, holds and restocks all day, so the words are ready when a message comes in. You still read each one and change the name or time before you send it.

Hi [first name]! I put the [item] in [size] aside for you. I’ll keep it until [day and time]. Just let me know if you’re coming by.
Thanks for asking! That one is sold out in [size] right now. I can let you know if it comes back in. Want me to do that?
Hi [first name]! New pieces are arriving [day]. I’ll post them on Instagram as soon as they’re out on the racks.
Yes, you’re welcome to stop by and try it on. We’re in the shop [days and hours]. See you soon!
Thank you so much, [first name]! I’m so glad you love it. Come say hi next time you’re near.

steps.title: Your Instagram captions, said out loud, finished as text
steps.read: You say what you need out loud, and ChatGPT turns it into a finished Instagram caption in your voice. You talk it through the way you would tell a customer about a new piece, so it comes out sounding like you. You read it and fix anything before it goes up.

material.label: Your opening line
items: I own a small women’s clothing boutique. I’m going to tell you out loud about a new piece or a sale, and I want you to turn what I say into an Instagram caption for my shop. Keep it warm, short and friendly, like me chatting with a regular customer. Three to four sentences, with a simple line at the end that tells people how to reach me or stop by. Use only the details I say, like the item, color, sizes and any hold or pickup details. Never add prices, fabrics, dates or claims I did not mention. If something seems missing, put it in square brackets and tell me what to fill in. Give back just the finished caption, ready for me to read and change.

material.label: What to say
items: The item and its color
The sizes we have, and if any are low
The price, only if I want it in the post
Anything special, like new arrival, last one or sale
How people can get it, like message me, DM or stop by the shop
The mood I want, like fun, simple or cozy

safeUse: Never type a customer’s full name, phone number, address or payment details into ChatGPT. Use square brackets instead.
Don’t paste in private messages with names showing. Take the names out first.
Don’t type in your sales numbers, supplier prices or bank details.
Read every reply and caption before it goes out, and check sizes, colors and hold times against your real stock.
Use your own words for store hours and policies, and never let ChatGPT guess them.

design.today: You answer customer messages many times a day, each one from scratch. They come in by Instagram DMs, text messages, phone calls and in person, and you work on your phone only.
design.newWay: Your most common replies, like holding a size until a set time or confirming what is in stock, are saved on your phone and a few letters bring each one up. You still read and adjust every reply before it goes, filling in the dress, size and time. This fits a phone only day, where retyping the same answer many times a day is the part worth removing.

steps.goal: Pick your ten most common customer replies from your recent messages, such as holding an item, sizes in stock and opening hours.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you can use it to tidy your replies.
Turn your ten replies into short, friendly versions in your own voice with gaps for item, size and time.
Save the ten replies so each one is a few letters away in any chat or DM.

design.today: You write Instagram captions every week, usually from scratch.
design.newWay: You keep a saved assistant that knows your boutique's voice. For each new post you tell it what the piece is and anything worth saying, either typed or spoken, and it gives you a caption draft in your style. You change it and post it yourself, so captions sound like you without starting from a blank page each week.
